about: The Magic of Lights page for Daytona lists the show at 1801 W International Speedway Blvd and gives a season of November 20, 2026 through January 2, 2027. Hours are posted as nightly, 6 PM to 10 PM. This listing shows nightly dates from November 27 to December 24, and the show continues after that through January 2.

Pricing is by vehicle, not by person. A standard car weekday ticket (Monday to Thursday) is $33.99 online and $37 at the gate, and a standard any-day ticket is $36.99 online and $42 at the gate. A limo or party bus any-day ticket is $49.99 online and $58 at the gate. A Dash Pass to skip the line is $54.99 online and $58 at the gate, and a standard season pass is listed at $89.99 per vehicle.
A November-only price of $20 per vehicle ($25 at the gate) appears on the page. Since this listing begins on November 27, that deal applies only to the last few November nights.

Visitor reviews on the page mention seeing Santa, making s'mores, trees that change color with music, and hot cocoa and roasted marshmallows at a Holiday Village. The host page itself shows only the words Holiday Village with a photo, so confirm what is offered on the night you go.
Tickets are sold through Tixr, and a link is on this page. Because you drive through, the show suits toddlers and anyone who prefers to stay warm and seated.
faq: How long does Magic of Lights Daytona run?
November 20, 2026 to January 2, 2027, nightly from 6 PM to 10 PM.
Where is it?
Daytona International Speedway, 1801 W International Speedway Blvd, Daytona Beach.
How much is a ticket?
Standard car tickets are $33.99 on weekdays and $36.99 any day online, charged per vehicle. November visits are $20 per vehicle.
Is it a drive-through?
Yes, the host describes a drive-through holiday lights experience.
Where do I buy tickets?
Through Tixr, linked from the host page.
Is there a season pass?
Yes, a standard car season pass is listed at $89.99 per vehicle.
Can I skip the line?
The host sells a Dash Pass for $54.99 per vehicle online.
Is there a weekday discount?
Yes. Monday to Thursday standard car tickets are $33.99 online.

about: The Daytona Beach area tourism calendar describes the 67th Annual Holly Hill Christmas Tree Lighting as one of the town's most cherished traditions, held on the front steps of City Hall. It runs Friday, December 4, 2026, from 6 PM to 7 PM.
The listing names three things to expect: holiday cheer, festive performances and a special visit from Santa Claus. It invites the whole family and says the event is free and open to all.

City Hall is at 1065 Ridgewood Avenue, the same address where the Holly Hill Christmas Parade ends the next morning. A family could attend the tree lighting on Friday evening and return Saturday for the parade.
The tree lighting is listed with a one hour window, so it works well for a weeknight with younger children.
Holly Hill sits just north of Daytona Beach along US 1. The Daytona Beach tourism calendar lists the City of Holly Hill as the presenter, and it numbers this the 67th annual lighting.
On Saturday the parade begins on Ridgewood Avenue at 5th Street and heads north to City Hall, so the building that hosts Friday's lighting is also the parade's finish line.
Plan for a short, simple evening. The listing gives only one hour, from 6 PM to 7 PM, and mentions performances and Santa without a detailed schedule.

If you are staying in the Daytona Beach area, the city of Daytona Beach also holds a Children's Christmas Party on Friday, December 11, at Jackie Robinson Ballpark, free for children, and its Christmas Parade follows on December 12.
The South Daytona tree lighting happens earlier, on Wednesday, December 2, at 6 PM in Central Park, so a family can see more than one lighting in the same week.

Anyone coming from out of town should note that Holly Hill City Hall sits on Ridgewood Avenue, which is US 1. The tourism calendar says both sides of US 1 close during the parade on Saturday, so Friday evening is the quieter way to visit.
faq: When is the Holly Hill tree lighting?
Friday, December 4, 2026, from 6 PM to 7 PM.
Where is it?
On the front steps of Holly Hill City Hall, 1065 Ridgewood Avenue.
Is Santa there?
Yes, the listing promises a special visit from Santa Claus.
Is it free?
Yes, free and open to all.
How is it different from the parade?
The tree lighting is Friday evening, and the parade is Saturday morning, December 5.
What is the host?
The City of Holly Hill, presented through the Daytona Beach area tourism calendar.
Does the town hold anything else that weekend?
Yes. The Holly Hill Christmas Parade follows on Saturday, December 5, starting at 10 AM.
Is there a theme for the weekend?
The parade has the theme Holly Jolly Hollydays, per the tourism calendar.
Is it near Daytona Beach?
Yes, Holly Hill is just north of Daytona Beach along US 1.
Is there another tree lighting nearby?
South Daytona holds its lighting on Wednesday, December 2, at 6 PM in Central Park.
Which evening is easier for young kids?
The tree lighting is a one hour evening event, while the parade starts at 10 AM Saturday.
Who runs the event?
The City of Holly Hill.

about: The Shores Resort and Spa in Daytona Beach Shores lists Breakfast with Santa at Azure Oceanfront Dining on Saturday, December 5, 2026. The breakfast buffet is served from 7 AM to 11 AM, and Santa's visit is listed from 9:30 AM to 11:30 AM.
The resort prices the breakfast at $24.99 per adult and $12.99 for children 12 and under. The buffet is described as festive, with seasonal favorites, family favorites and oceanfront views.
The event page says guests can expect photos, smiles and a little Christmas cheer with Santa. A Reserve Now link goes to OpenTable, though the page does not say a reservation is required.
The page does not print a street address. Look up The Shores Resort and Spa in Daytona Beach Shores before you go.
This is a restaurant buffet event, so the price covers a meal, which is different from the free community Santa events around Daytona Beach.
faq: When is Breakfast with Santa at Azure?
Saturday, December 5, 2026. Breakfast is 7 AM to 11 AM and Santa visits 9:30 AM to 11:30 AM.
How much does it cost?
$24.99 per adult and $12.99 for children 12 and under.
Do we need a reservation?
The page offers a Reserve Now link through OpenTable but does not say it is required.
Will there be photos with Santa?
The page mentions photos with Santa.
What kind of food is served?
A festive breakfast buffet with seasonal and family favorites.
Is it indoors?
It is held at Azure Oceanfront Dining, a restaurant with ocean views.

about: Volusia County Public Library describes S.T.R.E.A.M. as an interactive multi-literacy program that blends science, technology, reading, engineering, art and math. The program aims to build innovation, imagination, critical thinking and problem solving.
On December 14 the activity is ornament making. Children learn about the melting points of crayons and plastic as they design and create crayon speckled ornaments, according to the library listing.
The program runs from 3 PM to 4:30 PM in the Hope Place Library meeting room. The audience is listed as school age children, and the listing says no registration is required.
The Observer local news holiday guide places Hope Place Public Library at 1310 Wright Street in Daytona Beach and lists this program at 3 PM on Monday, December 14.
Supplies may be limited, so the library advises arriving early. A price is not shown on the listing.
The library calendar also lists Quick Crafts: Ornaments on December 10 at the Daytona Beach Regional Library, so families can choose between two ornament sessions.

Hope Place Public Library is the branch hosting this one. It also lists a Tech Time: Holiday Green Screen session on Monday, December 7, from 3 PM to 5 PM, where families choose a winter background and pose for a digital photo.
This ornament craft follows the school age pattern of the library's S.T.R.E.A.M. series. Each session introduces a small science idea and lets children make something to take home.

For a younger child, the Daytona Beach Regional Library lists Tiny Tots for preschoolers on December 15, and Quick Crafts: Ornaments on Thursday, December 10, from 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM for school age children (registration opens December 3 at 3:30 PM).

Families across Volusia can find similar sessions elsewhere. The Ormond Beach Regional Library lists Imagine and Explore: Holiday Workshop on Wednesday, December 16, at 3 PM, where children make cards, photo frames, keychains and ornaments and learn to wrap them.
The library's other Hope Place listing that week is a green screen photo session, so a family can plan a quick afternoon of ornaments at 3 PM on the 14th and photos the week before.
A craft like this suits a child who likes to tinker. Crayon pieces and plastic are the materials, and the lesson is how heat changes them, so the ornament doubles as a small science demonstration.
faq: Do we need to register?
No, the listing says no registration is required.
What age is it for?
School age children.
Where is it held?
The Hope Place Library meeting room, 1310 Wright Street, Daytona Beach.
What will kids make?
Crayon speckled ornaments, while learning about melting points.
What does it cost?
The listing does not show a price.
Are supplies limited?
Yes, the library says supplies may be limited.
Is there another ornament program?
Yes, Quick Crafts: Ornaments is December 10 at Daytona Beach Regional Library.
Is there a green screen program at Hope Place?
Yes, Tech Time: Holiday Green Screen is listed December 7 from 3 PM to 5 PM.
How long is the session?
One and a half hours, 3 PM to 4:30 PM.
Can toddlers go?
The audience listed is school age children.
Where else can kids make holiday gifts?
Ormond Beach Regional Library lists a holiday workshop on December 16 at 3 PM.

about: The LaunchPad is a space inside the Daytona Beach Regional Library, 105 Jackie Robinson Parkway. For this Spotlight program, the library schedules a holiday themed afternoon on Monday, December 14, from 2 PM to 4 PM.
The listing says participants will experience a holiday themed event through activities, games and craft making, using LaunchPad equipment, materials and games. The audience is listed as all ages.
No registration is required, according to the library. A price is not shown on the listing.
The same day, Hope Place Public Library hosts a holiday ornament program at 3 PM, and the Daytona Beach Regional Library lists Tiny Tots for preschoolers on December 15.
This is a library program, not a large festival, so expect a smaller crowd and a hands-on activity space.

Other Daytona Beach Regional Library holiday dates include Tech Time: Holiday Green Screen on Monday, December 7, from 10 AM to 4 PM, a music showcase with Tina and Barry from the Taylor Road Band on Tuesday, December 22, at 2 PM, and Noon Year's Eve on December 31 at 11:45 AM.
The library also lists Quick Crafts: Winter Magic Scratch Activity on Thursday, December 24, for school age children, with registration opening December 17 at 3:30 PM.
Parking and building details are not on the program listing. The Observer local news guide gives the library's street address as 105 Jackie Robinson Parkway.

Ormond Beach Regional Library has its own LaunchPad, which lists Arts and Crafts: Holiday Card on Saturday, December 5, for adults, and Arts and Crafts: Holiday Gift Tags on Monday, December 7, also for adults.
The library is a short drive from downtown Daytona Beach, where the parade follows a route along Beach Street south of Dr. Mary McLeod Bethune Boulevard to Jackie Robinson Parkway.

The program comes two days after the Daytona Beach Christmas Parade on Beach Street (Saturday, December 12) and three days after the city's free Children's Christmas Party at Jackie Robinson Ballpark (Friday, December 11), so it is a calmer weekday option once the weekend crowds are done.

Families who want something more structured the same afternoon can compare it with the 3 PM ornament program at Hope Place Public Library, which is for school age children and uses crayon melting as its science lesson.
